free_tier.stated: 2 GB storage + 10 GB bandwidth per month, unlimited repositories and unlimited CI/CD minutes. Private repositories are no longer usable on the free plan (restricted since 7 Sep 2023), so the free tier is effectively public-repo only.

egress.terms: 10 GB/month of download bandwidth; overage is $1.50/GB on paid plans and the account is disabled at the 'maximum overage amount' setting. So on Free it is a hard wall.

record.interface_detail: rest (packagecloud API), native apt/yum/ruby/pypi/npm clients via packagecloud.io/install/repositories/...
record.tooling: packagecloud CLI (`packagecloud push`), `curl -X POST` to the API, setup scripts for apt/yum; public repos pull anonymously.
record.chaining: Unlimited repositories per account, but storage and bandwidth are account-level watermarks ('high watermark for any given billing period'), so N repos do not multiply the 2 GB. Only N accounts would.

limits.value: bandwidth per month, unlimited repositories and unlimited CI/CD minutes

record.limits_note: 2 GB storage (high-water mark, so delete-then-reupload does not refund within a period); 10 GB/month bandwidth; private repos gated; packages over 2.6 GB are a paid-plan feature; bandwidth metered from request logs, HEAD/conditional GETs excluded.
record.reliability_note: Stable hosted service; the 2023 change that cut private repos off the free plan shows the free tier is a moving target.

evidence.proved: read live (firecrawl render): 'Free ... 10 GB bandwidth ... 2 GB storage ... Unlimited CI/CD Minutes'; comparison table shows 'Unlimited repositories', 'Public repositories' ticked, 'Private repositories' and 'Package sizes > 2.6 GB' as paid
read live: 'if you upload 100GB of packages, and delete 90GB of them, you'll still have used 100GB for that billing period' (high-water mark)
read live: free-plan private repos got 402s from 7 Sep 2023
